records.content: FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Young adult follow-up attendance was lower than the older participant group in the April monitoring review.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Reminder messages were associated with mixed follow-up attendance across two programme sites; this record does not establish why.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Some young adult participants described travel cost and appointment timing as barriers to follow-up.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Staff observed that peer introductions sometimes increased return visits, but notes were not systematically collected.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: A small anonymous survey reported that several young adults preferred flexible follow-up contact.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: A partner reported stable engagement among a small young adult outreach group, using a different attendance definition.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Older participants had more consistent scheduled follow-up than the young adult group during the same period.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Some participants said reminders were useful, while others said message access was inconsistent.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: One monthly register was incomplete and cannot support a complete comparison.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Evening contact options were requested, but no demographic breakdown was recorded.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: A youth employment partner used trusted peer intermediaries for follow-up engagement; transferability is unknown.
FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION: Survey participation was voluntary and may not represent participants who stopped attending.
